goal: Produce phlex-design/phlex-art-comparison-report.md: a comprehensive report for the Phlex design team comparing Art and Phlex persistent references, addressing (1) how Art/Phlex differences should shape a Phlex-native C++ manifestation of persistent references, (2) what algorithm use of art::Ptr/art::Assns/art::Find{One,Many}{,P} looks like in a Phlex iteration and how much explicit Phlex machinery users must touch, (3) enumerated categories of in-Art LArSoft algorithm changes that ease Phlex migration without altering data products while keeping the migration verifiable, and (4) remaining migration steps after the in-Art steps.
notes: Large read-heavy research + single-document synthesis task. Structured as gated phases so the execute orchestrator can run/resume within its step budget. Exploration steps are read-only and parallelizable; each emits a compact structured evidence brief (file:line anchors + quoted snippets) rather than raw dumps, to protect context. Art and LArSoft framework sources are NOT available locally (only spack recipes in ~/work/fnal_art); those steps must fetch canonical headers/modules from GitHub (art-framework-suite/canvas, LArSoft/larana,lardataobj) via webfetch and MUST cite retrieved URLs. Phlex framework, phlex-design docs, and phlex-examples/migration ARE local under ~/work/{phlex,phlex-design,phlex-examples} and should be read directly. Steering constraints to honor in synthesis: phlex-design/ non-doc/ files (incl. persistent-references-and-associations.md) are non-authoritative thoughts; the algorithm-facing C++ representation of Phlex persistent references is deliberately unspecified and this report contributes to it; LArSoft algorithms are representative-not-exemplary; persistent-references-and-associations.md covers only the backend-agnostic on-disk description aspect. Gate G1 checkpoints evidence sufficiency before analysis; gate G2 checkpoints analysis coverage before final synthesis.

steps.description: coder-qwen sub-agent (litellm default): Read the local Phlex framework identity/reference substructure to characterize what Phlex already offers as building blocks for a persistent reference. Read ~/work/phlex/phlex/model/{data_cell_index,product_specification,handle,identifier,data_cell_counts,products,product_store}.{hpp,cpp} and phlex/phlex/model/fwd.hpp. Produce a compact structured brief: for each type, its role, public API surface relevant to references (constructors, accessors, comparison/hashing, serialization hooks), and how data_cell_index + product_specification + element index together could form the persistent-reference triple. Do NOT dump whole files; quote only the decisive declarations with file:line anchors.
steps.output: Evidence brief E1: Phlex in-memory identity model (types, APIs, gaps) with file:line anchors, suitable for grounding a Phlex-native persistent-reference design.
steps.self_check: Brief names data_cell_index, product_specification, and handle and states whether each is persistable; cites at least 6 file:line anchors.

steps.description: coder-qwen sub-agent (litellm default): Read the local Phlex HOF/algorithm programming model and the mock-workflow association usage to characterize how a user's algorithm currently receives inputs and returns products, and how associations are represented today. Read ~/work/phlex/test/mock-workflow/{types.hpp,largeant.cpp,algorithm.hpp,ion_and_scint.cpp,three_tuple_algorithm.cpp} and the phlex module/registration + HOF entry points (grep ~/work/phlex/phlex for module.hpp, transform/fold/unfold registration, PHLEX_REGISTER_ALGORITHMS, handle<>, and 'association'). Produce a compact structured brief: the shape of a Phlex algorithm signature (tuple-in/tuple-out, families, handle<T>), how products are named/labeled, and the current association<A,B,D> placeholder and its usage in largeant.cpp. Quote decisive lines with file:line anchors only.

steps.description: reason model: Evidence-sufficiency gate. Review briefs E1-E6 for coverage, consistency, provenance hygiene (authoritative vs non-authoritative; local-read vs webfetched-with-URL), and contradictions. Confirm the evidence can support all four report questions: (Q1) Art/Phlex differences -> Phlex-native ref C++ design; (Q2) algorithm-level before/after and how much explicit Phlex machinery leaks to users; (Q3) enumerable in-Art LArSoft change categories that preserve data products + Art functionality while easing migration and preserving verifiability; (Q4) remaining post-in-Art migration steps. Emit either PASS with a short gap-free confirmation, or FAIL with a specific list of missing evidence and which step id must be re-run/extended.
steps.output: Gate verdict PASS/FAIL with enumerated gaps mapped to step ids; on FAIL, concrete re-run instructions.
steps.self_check: Verdict explicitly maps available evidence to each of Q1-Q4 and flags any webfetch-blocked or missing-anchor briefs; FAIL includes actionable per-step remediation.

steps.description: reason model: Analyze Q1 — how differences between Art and Phlex (and its design) should influence a Phlex-native C++ manifestation of persistent references. Using E1,E2,E3,E5 (and E4,E6 as context), reason from the concrete divergences: Art's global mutable Event + ProductID/key handles vs Phlex's functional pure-operator HOFs, framework-owned product lifetime, arbitrary-depth data-layer hierarchy and data-cell coordinates, indexed families vs ordered sequences, concept-vs-concrete types + Translators, and framework-agnostic backend (FORM/HDF5). Derive design implications and options for the algorithm-facing C++ type(s): the reference triple <cell_coord?, product_spec_id, element_index?>; whether refs are values vs handles; cross-cell vs intra-cell defaults (phlex issue #75); how references compose with families and folds/unfolds; how a reference stays valid under Phlex's ownership model; and how associations-as-data-products differ from a transient FindManyP query view. Present 2-3 candidate C++ shapes with tradeoffs, explicitly noting which design points are currently UNSPECIFIED and that this analysis is a contribution, not a ratified decision. Cite evidence-brief anchors.
steps.output: Analysis A1: Q1 answer — evidence-grounded design implications and 2-3 candidate Phlex-native persistent-reference C++ shapes with tradeoffs, unspecified-points flagged.
steps.self_check: A1 ties each design implication to a specific Art/Phlex difference and to an evidence anchor, and explicitly labels currently-unspecified design decisions.

steps.description: reason model: Analyze Q2 — what an algorithm's use of art::Ptr/art::Assns/art::Find{One,Many}{,P} looks like in a Phlex iteration, and the extent to which users must invoke explicit Phlex programming constructs. Using E2,E4,E5,E6 and the candidate shapes from A1, write concrete before/after C++ sketches for a representative producer (create hits + hit<->wire association) and a representative consumer (recover wire from a hit) mapping each Art construct to its Phlex counterpart: produces<Assns> -> returning an association product in the output tuple; art::Ptr -> the Phlex reference value; FindManyP -> either a framework-provided query view or an explicit join over families. Explicitly quantify/enumerate the explicit Phlex machinery the user must touch in each candidate (labels, handle<>, family indices, translators, registration) and where the framework can hide it. Cite anchors.
steps.output: Analysis A2: Q2 answer — before/after producer+consumer C++ sketches and an explicit enumeration of user-visible Phlex machinery per candidate design.
steps.self_check: A2 contains paired Art-vs-Phlex code sketches for both a producer and a consumer, and an explicit list of the Phlex constructs the user must write for each candidate.

steps.description: reason model: Analyze Q3 and Q4. Q3: enumerate CATEGORIES of change that can be made to LArSoft algorithms while (a) preserving in-Art functionality and (b) not altering data products, that nonetheless ease Phlex migration and keep as much of the process verifiable-in-Art as possible. Ground categories in E4 and E6 (e.g., isolating pure computational cores from Event/Handle access; replacing framework-ref dereferences with parameters carrying the referenced data or intrinsic domain keys; hoisting produces/get boilerplate behind thin adapters; making association production a distinct, testable step; removing incidental Event/ServiceHandle coupling; standardizing input/output as plain-old-data passable to a pure function). For each category: mechanism, why it is Art-behavior-preserving and product-preserving, how it is verified in Art (e.g., compare_hits.py-style regression vs recorded outputs), and how it shortens the eventual Phlex step. Q4: outline the REMAINING migration steps after the in-Art changes — wiring the pure core into a Phlex HOF, expressing references/associations in the chosen Phlex representation, configuring the data-layer hierarchy/families, providing translators/FORM IDL for persistence, and the reduced cross-framework verification that remains. Cite anchors.
steps.output: Analysis A3: Q3 enumerated, verifiable, product-preserving in-Art change categories + Q4 remaining post-in-Art Phlex migration steps, evidence-anchored.
steps.self_check: A3 lists distinct Q3 categories each with a preservation rationale AND an in-Art verification method, and a Q4 step sequence that begins where the in-Art work ends.

steps.description: reason model: Analysis-coverage gate. Verify A1,A2,A3 fully and consistently answer Q1-Q4, remain faithful to steering constraints (non-authoritative sources flagged; unspecified design decisions labeled as contributions not decisions; LArSoft treated as representative), and contain no unsupported claims (each key claim traceable to E1-E6 anchors). Emit PASS with a brief confirmation, or FAIL listing specific deficiencies mapped to analysis step ids to re-run.
steps.output: Gate verdict PASS/FAIL with per-analysis-step remediation on FAIL.
steps.self_check: Verdict confirms each of Q1-Q4 is answered and steering constraints are respected, or specifies exactly which analysis step to redo and why.

steps.description: litellm/azure/claude-opus-4-8 (more capable model required for long-form authoritative synthesis): Write the final comprehensive report to ~/work/phlex-design/phlex-art-comparison-report.md for the Phlex design team and its lead. Integrate A1,A2,A3 and evidence E1-E6 into a single coherent Markdown document. Required structure: (1) Executive summary with a clear recommendation stance and explicit statement that the algorithm-facing Phlex reference C++ representation is currently unspecified and this report is a design contribution, not a ratified decision; (2) Background: Art vs Phlex framework models and the persistent-reference problem; (3) Q1 — Art/Phlex differences and their implications for a Phlex-native C++ reference, with the 2-3 candidate shapes + tradeoffs table; (4) Q2 — before/after algorithm code sketches and an explicit accounting of user-visible Phlex machinery per candidate; (5) Q3 — enumerated in-Art, product-preserving, verifiable LArSoft change categories; (6) Q4 — remaining post-in-Art migration steps; (7) Open questions / recommendations to the design lead. Attribute non-authoritative inputs as such (esp. persistent-references-and-associations.md scoped to on-disk description; other phlex-design/ root docs as non-authoritative), keep code sketches concrete, and preserve source anchors (local file:line and cited GitHub URLs) inline or in a references section. Respect repo formatting: single trailing newline, no trailing whitespace, markdownlint rules MD012/MD022/MD031/MD032/MD034/MD040 (fenced code blocks carry language tags, bare URLs wrapped, blank lines around headings/lists/code fences).
steps.output: The complete report written to phlex-design/phlex-art-comparison-report.md answering Q1-Q4 with candidate designs, code sketches, enumerated change categories, remaining steps, and a references/anchors section.
